score.doctor_diagnosis: Focal (temporal lobe) epilepsy with impaired awareness, non-lesional, presenting with gustatory aura, automatisms, and post-ictal confusion.
score.doctor_final_text:
Doctor: Good news — no structural cause on MRI. Based on the aura, hand automatisms, confusion afterward, and EEG findings, this points to focal (temporal lobe) epilepsy, likely non-lesional.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Focal (temporal lobe) epilepsy with impaired awareness, non-lesional, presenting with gustatory aura, automatisms, and post-ictal confusion.

dialogue.text: Can you tell me more about these episodes — how long do they last, and how often do they happen?
They last about 3 or 4 minutes each time. It's been happening pretty often this past month - maybe a few times, but I'm not really sure exactly how many because I don't remember them happening.
Do you notice anything before an episode starts, like an unusual smell, taste, or feeling — an "aura"?
Yes, actually! Right before it happens, I get this weird muddy taste in my mouth. It's really strange and then I don't remember anything after that.
Does anyone who's witnessed these episodes mention how long it takes you to become fully alert and act normal again afterward?
My brother said I seemed really tired and confused for a while after. Mom says it takes me maybe 10 or 15 minutes before I'm really back to normal and can answer questions properly.
Do you ever bite your tongue, lose bladder control, or have jerking movements during these episodes, based on what witnesses have told you?
My brother said he saw me making some hand gestures during one of them, but I don't think anyone mentioned anything about biting my tongue or wetting myself.
Doctor: Have you had any head injuries, family history of epilepsy or seizures, or been under unusual stress or sleep deprivation recently?

No, I haven't hit my head or anything like that. I don't think anyone in my family has had seizures before. I've been sleeping okay and school's been pretty normal - nothing really stressful going on.
Doctor: Have you had an EEG or MRI before, and would you be open to getting one now so we can look at your brain activity more closely?
No, I've never had any tests like that done before. I guess that would be okay if it helps figure out what's going on with me.
RESULTS: Electroencephalogram (EEG) shows interictal spikes and sharp waves localized to the temporal lobes, more prominent on the right side.

Doctor: That EEG finding fits with the aura, automatisms, and post-episode confusion you described — this looks like focal seizures arising from the temporal lobe. I'd like to get an MRI of your brain to check for a structural cause before we finalize things.
